title: Drought intensifies rhizosphere priming and reduces soil organic carbon stability in a subtropical forest
abstract: We conducted a long-term drought experiment in a subtropical forest to test how root exudates mediate rhizosphere priming and soil organic carbon stability. Drought increased root exudation and microbial decomposition, revealing a mechanism that weakens mineral-associated organic carbon.

title: Soil-derived microbiomes shape host fitness across contrasting environments
abstract: A multi-omics experiment combined metagenomics and metabolomics to identify soil-derived generalist bacteria that influence host fitness. Transplant experiments revealed microbial mechanisms linking soil biodiversity to ecosystem health.

title: A framework for carbon-neutral land systems under climate change
abstract: This review proposes a new framework for carbon neutrality that integrates ecosystem carbon sinks, land management and climate adaptation. It evaluates policy scenarios and identifies key uncertainties for sustainable development.

title: Phosphorus recycling in rice roots depends on a nitric oxide pathway
abstract: A combination of mutant analysis and isotope tracing tested phosphorus recycling in rice roots. The study reveals a nitric oxide dependent pathway and provides a target for improving nutrient-use efficiency in agriculture.

title: Environmental monitoring for sustainable urban health
abstract: High-resolution monitoring and machine learning were used to assess environmental exposure and health risks in cities. The framework supports early warning and spatial planning.

title: Remote spectral detection of canopy functional dimensions
abstract: Using airborne remote sensing and field observations, this study detected canopy functional dimensions across forest types. A novel trait-based framework links spectral diversity to ecosystem resilience.

title: Home-range dissimilarity and trait coordination during range expansion
abstract: A large field survey examined trait coordination and home-range ecological dissimilarity during plant establishment. The results advance community assembly theory and inform restoration decisions.

title: Coupling and coordination of climate and vegetation on a rapidly greening plateau
abstract: The study combined satellite indicators, climate data and statistical models to evaluate climate-vegetation coupling. It provides an operational assessment tool for ecological restoration and policy evaluation.

title: Global synthesis of warming effects on ecosystem carbon feedbacks
abstract: A global synthesis and meta-analysis quantify warming effects on carbon feedbacks. The work identifies nonlinear thresholds and highlights climate mitigation priorities.

title: Mycorrhizal networks regulate belowground carbon allocation
abstract: Isotope tracing and a manipulative experiment reveal how mycorrhizal networks regulate belowground carbon allocation and plant-soil-microbe interactions.

title: Machine learning predicts biodiversity responses to land-use change
abstract: A machine-learning framework integrates global biodiversity observations to predict responses to land-use change and guide conservation planning.
